steps.say: Hands are growing clumsy with buttons and jars while gait is turning unsteady. Hoffman flick, inverted brachioradialis, Babinski and Lhermitte electric shocks are completing the picture. Bladder urgency is arriving late.
steps.tx: Degenerative cervical myelopathy presents with **hand clumsiness**, buttoning difficulty, unsteady gait and bladder urgency, with Hoffman sign, inverted brachioradialis, Babinski and Lhermitte signs on examination. Neck pain may be absent while hands fail. The pattern is upper motor neuron below the neck with lower motor neuron at compressed roots.

steps.say: Severity is scored out of eighteen on the mJOA scale across motor, sensory and bladder domains. Below twelve is severe disease and twelve to fourteen is moderate. Above fourteen is mild and it is watched closely.
steps.tx: The **mJOA score** (modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association) grades severity out of 18, with below 12 severe myelopathy, 12 to 14 moderate and above 14 mild disease guiding surgical urgency. Motor, sensory and bladder subscores add to the total. The number is tracked at every visit.

steps.say: Moderate, severe or progressive disease is operated without delay. Mild still disease is watched with serial scores and scans. One in five mild cases is deteriorating, so follow-up is strict.
steps.tx: Moderate, severe or **progressive myelopathy** is operated, while mild non-progressive disease is watched with serial mJOA and MRI because one in 5 deteriorate. Progression on any visit converts watch to surgery. Stable mild disease earns continued observation. Counselling covers both paths at diagnosis.

steps.say: Short kyphotic disease is approached from the front with discectomy or corpectomy. Multilevel stenosis with preserved lordosis is handled from behind with laminoplasty. Alignment is deciding the route.
steps.tx: **Anterior discectomy fusion** (ACDF) or corpectomy suits 1 to 2 level disease with kyphosis, while posterior laminoplasty or laminectomy-fusion suits multilevel stenosis with preserved lordosis. Kyphosis needs anterior correction; lordosis tolerates posterior drift. The wrong route risks failed decompression. Imaging decides before positioning.

steps.say: Ossified posterior longitudinal ligament is common in East Asian patients. Massive anterior bars are floated or resected from the front. Extreme canal occupancy is decompressed from behind instead.
steps.tx: Ossified posterior longitudinal ligament (**OPLL**) is common in East Asian patients and produces massive anterior compression, managed anteriorly by floating or resection and posteriorly when the canal occupancy is extreme. The floating technique thins the bar and lets it drift forward. Dural ossification raises the cerebrospinal fluid leak risk.

steps.say: Bright cord signal with dark T1 change is marking irreversible injury at the compressed level. Recovery after surgery is then incomplete. The finding is strengthening the case against delay, not for waiting.
steps.tx: MRI **T2 hyperintensity** with T1 hypointensity at the compressed level marks irreversible cord injury and predicts incomplete recovery, strengthening the case against delay. T2 signal alone may be oedema, but T2 bright with T1 dark means myelomalacia. Operate before the signal turns dark on T1. Document the signal in every report.

steps.say: Root pain is following a dermatomal strip down the arm with a positive Spurling test. Most cases are settling like sciatica with collars and therapy. Persistent deficit is earning foraminotomy or fusion.
steps.tx: Cervical radiculopathy with dermatomal pain down the arm and a positive **Spurling test** is managed like lumbar sciatica first, with foraminotomy or ACDF for persistent root deficit. The map of thumb, middle and little finger localises the root level. Weakness lasting weeks forces the decision.

vis.caption: Dermatome landmarks map root pain to its spinal level for Spurling-positive radiculopathy. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Deltoid weakness after surgery is signalling C5 palsy and it is watched for months. Swallowing and voice are checked before discharge. Most palsies are resolving with therapy and time.
steps.tx: Postoperative **C5 palsy** with deltoid weakness, drip and dysphagia after anterior surgery, and hoarseness from recurrent laryngeal traction are the counselled complications. C5 palsy typically appears days after a good operation. Reassurance with physiotherapy sees most through. Warn every patient before consent.
